 Follow See the Extreme Effects of the Bay Area's Record-Breaking Storm
 SF Gate Fri, November 20, 2026 at 10:34 AM UTC Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. A powerful storm brought parts of the Bay Area to a standstill Wednesday, flooding roads and stranding cars. San Francisco broke a 108-year daily rainfall record, marking the sixth-wettest November day ever recorded in the city as heavy rain swept through. The low-pressure system, driven by a cold front from the northwest Pacific Ocean, delivered the season's heaviest rainfall and strongest winds. Showers began in the North Bay before reaching San Francisco and the rest of the region in the early morning. By 9 a.m., the National Weather Service had issued a flood advisory for much of the Bay Area. San Francisco received 1.73 inches in just three hours. Videos showed stalled cars surrounded by water erupting from maintenance holes on flooded roads. Downtown San Francisco edged past November's monthly rainfall average of 2.60 inches. But the city remained far from its wettest November on record: in 1885, a total of 11.75 inches of rain fell during the month.
